Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited about Redwood's performance. Procurement asked me to send our initial redlines for the MSA and the Order Form so legal and finance can sync. I've attached a PDF with track changes for the MSA and a short spreadsheet with our preferred billing cadence.

High-level asks:
- Limit telemetry retention to 12 months for analytics data (Section 6.2).
- Clarify that Redwood will not use customer payload for model training; add explicit language in Data Use section.
- Add a 60-day ramp credit if committed capacity baseline is missed (we can discuss thresholds).

We'd like to get to an agreed set of redlines by EOD Friday, 19 Aug if possible — procurement has an internal board meeting on 23 Aug. Please loop in legal/finance.

Thanks Steph and Natalie. I reviewed the MSA PDF and added technical/legal comments — attaching an annotated MSA and a short summary of our positions. Short notes here: 

1) Data use / model training (Section 5.1 in their doc): we can agree to a prohibition on using customer payload for continuous model training for BrightBridge-specific data, with the following carveouts:
  - Aggregated telemetry and anonymized service metrics (latency, error rates, system health) are necessary for reliability and will be retained; we can cap retention for analytics metrics at 12 months per their ask.
  - We cannot exclude use of synthetic or public datasets in general model improvements; we will add explicit language stating customer payload won't be used for proprietary training without written consent.

2) Telemetry retention (Section 6.2): we'll accept 12 months for analytics/observability metrics. Operational logs required for security investigations and compliance (e.g., audit logs) may need longer retention; propose a two-line carveout that audit logs retention follows the regulatory schedule and will be disclosed in Exhibit X.

3) Ramp credit: the 60-day credit ask is operationally large. Proposed compromise: a 30-day usage credit triggerable if committed baseline is missed for 2 consecutive months during the ramp period, with explicit definitions of baseline measurements and mitigation steps (notifications, throttling). Finance will need to sign off.

4) SOW scope edit: the SOW references "batch batching optimizations" — ambiguous. Suggest clarifying expected throughput (tokens/sec or inference QPS), expected latency P50/P95, and the acceptance test for go-live. This will avoid scope creep and makes billing triggers clearer.

I'm attaching: BrightBridge_MSA_annotated_20270816.pdf (comments), and a one-pager summary: BB_redline_summary_20270816.docx (text).

Natalie — if you can confirm whether audit logs are a hard requirement for them at >12 months, that would help.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, Natalie Park <natalie.park@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightBridge - MSA & Order Form redlines

Thanks — quick finance read. I've reviewed their proposed billing cadence in BB_billing_pref_20270812.xlsx and put a model in the attached spreadsheet: OrderForm_BB_fee_proposal_20270818.xlsx. Key points: 

- 60-day ramp credit as a full-billing-month rebate is too broad; it could be materially dilutive if they have burst patterns. Our proposed 30-day credit (pro-rated against missed baseline) is manageable.
- We need to lock the billing measurement (UTC hour intervals, p95 over the billing window) — otherwise reconciliation will be messy.
- If they want a longer telemetry retention for audit logs, that should not change billing but will require written justification and a security review (costs may apply).
- Suggest a flexible payment term: Net 30 for initial 6 months, then Net 45 for committed customers; keeps cashflow predictable for us.

I've attached the spreadsheet and highlighted the cells where the credit math is shown. Laura

Attachments: OrderForm_BB_fee_proposal_20270818.xlsx

Hi Natalie — thanks for the patience. Quick consolidated update and proposed path forward so BrightBridge's board can see progress ahead of 23 Aug: 

1) Legal positions (Karthik):
   - We will accept a prohibition on customer payload for model training absent explicit consent; we'll add a clause and confirm aggregator telemetry retention at 12 months.
   - Audit logs: we'll add an Exhibit that documents audit-log retention and the exception for security/compliance investigations. Please confirm if BrightBridge requires >12 months for audit logs.

2) Finance (Laura):
   - Proposed compromise on ramp credit: 30-day pro-rated credit if baseline missed for 2 consecutive months during the first 3 months post-go-live. Measurement details to be added to Exhibit B (UTC hour windows, p95 over billing window).
   - Initial payment terms: Net 30 for first 6 months, then Net 45 on committed renewal.

3) SOW clarity (Priyom):
   - Priyom will propose concrete throughput/latency acceptance criteria for Exhibit C so we can link billing triggers to measurable metrics.

Action items / attachments: 
- Attached: BrightBridge_combined_redline_20270820.pdf (annotated MSA combining legal comments + finance notes)
- Priyom will share a proposed SOW excerpt (throughput/latency acceptance and test plan) by Mon 23 Aug.
- Natalie: can you confirm whether audit logs >12 months are required by your compliance team? Also confirm whether your board meeting can accept a conditional agreement subject to finalization of Exhibit C details.

If we get a yes on conditional approval, legal will prepare a clean MSA with tracked Exhibit C to sign. If you prefer to redline further, we can loop your counsel directly.

Thanks — I'll monitor and escalate if we need exec sign-off.
